children: CEO Hiroo Ota has played down the prospect of deeper ties with South Korea’s SK Hynix
, citing antitrust concerns and the Japanese memory-chip maker’s existing manufacturing arrangements with SanDisk

Bloomberg reported that Ota also said Kioxia would seek to prevent memory prices from rising too sharply, warning that higher prices could hurt demand for AI products over the longer term. He said prices had already risen enough and told the company’s sales teams not to push for substantially higher prices.
Kioxia makes NAND memory chips used for data storage and is a key supplier as companies race to expand AI infrastructure.

SK Hynix is a major Kioxia shareholder and has been linked with the Japanese company in speculation over closer manufacturing ties. The two companies are also working together on memory technology. But Ota said closer cooperation would face antitrust hurdles and would be difficult to reconcile with Kioxia’s existing manufacturing arrangements with Sandisk.
“We can’t just say, 'Well then, let’s make it three companies,'” Ota said of a hypothetical Kioxia-SK Hynix-Sandisk manufacturing tie-up in an interview with Bloomberg News.
